milestone.title: raul TUI mode enum dispatch + action/command pattern

intent.outcome: raul's TUI replaces the giant inline match chain in runner.rs (~450 lines mixing global keys, tab-bar focus, lane-specific logic, and command dispatch) with a Mode enum + per-mode handler functions. The dispatcher becomes a small top-level function: 'given this mode and this key, return a Vec<Action>'. Adding a new mode (Board, Detail, Input, Help, Settings — required for M140) is a clean additive change.

problem.description: crates/raul/src/tui/runner.rs:132-218 contains a giant inline match chain that mixes concerns: global keys (q, Q, Esc, b, Tab) are checked before is_input_active(); input mode only handles Esc/Enter/Backspace/Char; tab_bar_focused routes to handle_tab_bar_key; lane-specific logic inlines Board special cases (Left/Right/Char('r')) and then falls through to handle_event(); handle_event() then has its own massive match on (ContentState, Event) pairs. Hard to test, hard to extend, easy to forget a path. herdr's src/app/input/ has 13 mode-specific sub-modules (terminal.rs, modal.rs, mouse.rs, navigate.rs, selection.rs, copy_mode.rs, settings.rs, overlays.rs, sidebar.rs, …) and an exhaustive Mode enum of 17 variants. The dispatcher is small; the work lives in per-mode handlers.

in_scope: New Mode enum in crates/raul/src/tui/mode.rs: Normal, Input, Help, AnnotationThread, ReviewMenu, Settings, plus any other current 'inline-mode' state currently scattered through runner.rs
Replace inline mode checks with active_mode: Mode field on App
New module crates/raul/src/tui/modes/ with one file per mode (normal.rs, input.rs, help.rs, settings.rs, …) each exporting handle_key(mode, key, app) -> Vec<Action>

New Action enum in crates/raul/src/tui/action.rs: Quit, Up, Down, Enter, OpenTab(id), SelectItem(id), CreateAnnotation(text), ApproveAnnotation(id), ResolveAnnotation(id), OpenSettings, OpenHelp, … — pure data, no side effects
New fn apply_action(app: &mut App, action: Action) that mutates App and shells out to mp — this is where the side effects live, separate from the dispatch
Top-level dispatch becomes ~20 lines: match (app.active_mode, key) -> dispatch

Tests: for each mode, a unit test that the handler returns the right action for a representative key set; for apply_action, a test that the right mp invocation (or App mutation) happens for each action
out_of_scope: Adding new user-facing features — this is a refactor of existing behavior
Keybinds from config (M138-M139) — Mode and Action are the data structures keybinds dispatch on, but key parsing and config loading are separate milestones
Settings TUI content (M140) — Settings mode is registered here; the actual settings menu/forms land in M140
Prefix mode (herdr's ctrl+b style) — not justified for raul today

acceptance_criteria.description: A Mode enum exists with one variant per distinct UI mode in raul (Normal, Input, Help, AnnotationThread, ReviewMenu, Settings — plus any inline state currently scattered in runner.rs). The App struct has an active_mode: Mode field. Grep test asserts no inline mode flags remain in runner.rs. NOTE on Settings: Mode::Settings is registered here as a variant, but its handler is a clean no-op stub (dispatches nothing, or shows a 'settings coming in M140' placeholder) until M140 fills it — so M136 landing before M140 does not leave a broken dispatch path.

steps.action: Create crates/raul/src/tui/mode.rs with Mode enum: Normal, Input, Help, AnnotationThread, ReviewMenu, Settings. Add active_mode: Mode to App in app.rs. Remove any inline mode flags (input_mode boolean, show_help, show_review_menu) and replace reads with active_mode match.

steps.action: Create crates/raul/src/tui/action.rs with Action enum covering all current user-intent mutations (Quit, Up, Down, Enter, OpenTab, SelectItem, CreateAnnotation, ApproveAnnotation, ResolveAnnotation, OpenSettings, OpenHelp, etc.). Delete the old Event enum from event.rs.
steps.done_when: Action enum exists; old Event enum is removed from event.rs.

steps.action: Implement apply_action(app: &mut App, action: Action) in action.rs. Move all side effects (load_data_for_lane, create_annotation shell-out, etc.) here. The function is the single place that mutates App and shells out to mp.
steps.done_when: apply_action is the only place that mutates App from dispatch; no mp shell-outs from per-mode handlers.

steps.action: Create crates/raul/src/tui/modes/ with normal.rs, input.rs, help.rs, settings.rs (plus any other current inline-mode state). Each exports handle_key(key, &App) -> Vec<Action> — pure, no I/O, no App mutation.
steps.done_when: Each mode has its own handle_key function; no per-mode handler calls MpRunner.

steps.action: Author crates/raul/tests/tui_modes.rs: per-mode unit tests asserting handle_key returns the right Action for representative key sets; apply_action tests asserting the right mp invocation or App mutation for each Action; grep test asserting no mp shell-out calls inside modes/.
steps.done_when: Test file exists; covers all 6 modes; covers apply_action for at least 5 Action variants.

steps.action: Run cargo test -p raul. Verify all existing tests still pass and the new tui_modes tests are green.
steps.done_when: cargo test -p raul exits 0; zero regressions.

findings.description: action.rs::apply_enter duplicates the entire Action::ConfirmCoApproval body in its ContentState::CoApproval arm instead of delegating. The sibling MilestoneDetail and AnnotationThread arms delegate via 'return apply_action(app, runner, Action::...)', and the CoApproval arm comment says 'Same as ConfirmCoApproval' yet inlines ~17 lines of identical logic (resolve/reopen_annotation + co_approval_approve + load_annotations + check_approval_status). Drift risk: if the confirm flow changes in one arm, the other silently diverges. Remediation: replace the inlined body with 'return apply_action(app, runner, Action::ConfirmCoApproval);'.

modes/normal.rs::handle_overview_lane_key has an 'is_help_active(app)' guard (first branch) that is unreachable post-M136. is_help_active checks app.active_mode == Mode::Help, but dispatch_key routes Mode::Help to modes::help::handle_key, never to modes::normal::handle_key. So handle_overview_lane_key (which only runs when active_mode == Normal) can never observe is_help_active == true. The doc comment even admits it is kept 'as a guard even though Mode::Help is the canonical help state'. This is dead defensive code that obscures the real key table in a refactor whose goal is clarity. Remediation: remove the is_help_active branch (and the now-unused is_help_active helper if nothing else uses it), leaving the r/R/?/fall-through match.

Action::GoBack is a dead variant. Its own doc comment states 'Currently no mode handler emits this action' and its apply_action arm just calls apply_esc(app, runner) — i.e. it is an alias for Action::Esc that nothing produces. Every exhaustive match on Action (including the tui_modes.rs::actions_have_required_variants exhaustiveness test) has to carry an arm for it. Keeping speculative 'forward-compatible for M140' variants violates YAGNI and undermines the milestone's goal of a clean, exhaustive action/command surface; M140 can re-add the variant when it actually wires a 'g' binding. Remediation: remove Action::GoBack, its apply_action arm, and its exhaustiveness-test entry.
